title: Mistral Financial - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
summary: Postmortem follow-up to the 2027-09-08 latency and error spike that impacted Mistral's customer-facing payment fraud scoring. Reviewed root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler misconfiguration), mitigations deployed, short-term rollback strategies, and next-gen reliability improvements including KV cache telemetry and canarying for dedicated nodes.
action_items: Riley Ortiz: Provide kernel-level profiler logs and raw latency histograms by 2027-09-17
Marcus Lee: Share Mistral's traffic pattern CSV and peak windows by 2027-09-16
Camila Torres: Schedule dedicated-node canary for Mistral test cluster w/ 2-week window by 2027-09-20
Jamie Chen: Send the incident report and SOC2/KMS integration notes to Priya by 2027-09-15
next_steps: Redwood to share full incident packet (logs, traces, sampling config)
Run a 48-hour controlled canary of dedicated nodes with prefix caching enabled
Customer to confirm acceptable spike window and SLA rollback thresholds
Joint follow-up call in 1 week to review canary results and mitigation plan
transcript:
Header: 2027-09-14 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Riley (Redwood SE), Camila (Redwood CSM), Sonia (Mistral Head of Platform), Marcus (Mistral SRE), Priya (Mistral Security), Evan (Mistral PM)

Summary (auto): quick follow-up to confirm RCA and next steps after last week's incident, align on mitigations and roadmap for reliability improvements.

00:00 Jamie: okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to — uh — do a quick postmortem follow-up, confirm what we shipped and the next steps, hope that time still works for folks
00:10 Sonia: yeah thanks, um, appreciate it. We just want clarity on root cause and what changes mean for our SLAs, like we had multiple merchants hit the 99th percentile latency on the scoring call and some timed out
00:25 Riley: totally. I'll run through the timeline again briefly, then what we patched. So on 2027-09-08 at ~14:37 UTC we saw a rapid increase in cold-starts and KV cache evictions correlated with a spike in burst traffic from their nightly batch plus an ad-hoc peak. That led to repeated model load thrash on our dedicated pool node set and autoscaler responded by adding nodes but with a lag — the lag plus cache misses caused token generation latencies to jump and some requests to hit the client-side timeout
:42 Marcus: can you repeat, uh, the cache eviction bit? our telemetry showed few errors but big latencies, not full 500s except for like 2%, mostly timeouts at the edge
01:00 Riley: sure, so the root is twofold: first, the prefix/KV cache policy for that dedicated pool was set to LRU with a relatively small cache window because of memory limits. when the nightly batch started it evicted useful prefixes; second, our autoscaler policy for dedicated nodes was conservative — min nodes set low for cost reasons and scale-up cooldown was 90s which delayed recovery. combined effect = increased model loads and repeated small-model checkpoints, lots of context reloads
01:28 Priya: from security, were there any data exposures when the cache evicted? we run strict PII rules and need to validate logs aren't leaking tokens or user data
01:40 Riley: no evidence of token leakage; our logs show eviction markers but the data in cache is hashed and encrypted at rest, keys handled via customer KMS. we'll include the KMS audit logs in the packet, but, um, no PII found in traces so far
01:58 Jamie: quick note — earlier we did a partial rollback to the stable model variant and turned on prefix caching for the affected customer which reduced CPU and improved tail latency within ~12 minutes on average
02:12 Sonia: right, we saw latency drop back but our SREs still saw occasional spikes during billing cutover windows
02:22 Evan: question — is the rollout rollback something you can automate on thresholds, like automatic fallback if 99p exceeds X ms?
02:35 Riley: yes, we can do automated fallback. We already have route-level policies for model variant fallback, and we can wire a policy that triggers on 99th percent > threshold for N minutes. that's in the console but requires permission and we should test in canary first
02:50 Marcus: about autoscaling, would increasing min nodes help or will that just cost us? we were optimizing cost and set low min capacity
03:02 Camila: there's a tradeoff, yes, min nodes reduces cold-start risk but costs more. short term we recommended a dynamic buffer for peak windows and a burst policy that's pre-warmed. long-term we want smarter autoscaler that uses predicted traffic windows (you provided CSV last week), and also smarter eviction heuristics so we don't evict prefixes that are likely to be used within X minutes
03:25 Sonia: can Redwood help with suggested settings? we want guidance — like specific numbers for min nodes and cache size given our 3M qps daily and 240tps peak
03:38 Riley: absolutely — we'll run simulated workloads against your traffic pattern and provide recommended configs: suggested min nodes, cache window size, and a quantization profile suggestion if you can accept the slight delta in output quality. we'll include cost delta estimates
03:55 Priya: from compliance perspective, we need the SOC2 report and KMS integration docs and an audit trail of any changes to config during that incident
04:05 Jamie: yes, Camila will attach SOC2 + KMS integration notes and the change log. we'll also include role changes and who issued manual rollback
04:16 Marcus: can we get profiler dumps? the flame graphs would help SRE triage
04:22 Riley: yes, I'll share the profiler and kernel-level metrics; note there's some noise in the samples because of aggregated tracing, we'll include raw histograms too
04:35 Sonia: also, why did the dedicated pool see so much thrash vs hosted? is it the node type? we were on T4-based nodes with slightly older drivers, could that be a factor?
04:48 Riley: good point — node selection is part. the affected pool was on a mixed GPU set and an older driver where some kernels fallbacked to less optimized paths, which increased per-token latency under load. we recommended a driver and CUDA patch which we pushed to the pool in the hotfix. that plus prefix cache change and temporary increase to min nodes brought stability
05:10 Evan: for long-term mitigation what's on the roadmap? we heard mention of telemetry, better canarying, and KV cache improvements
05:18 Riley: roadmap items we discussed: 1) enhanced KV cache telemetry and hit/miss tagging per-prefix, 2) predictive autoscaler that ingests historical CSV windows, 3) canarying for dedicated-node kernel/driver changes with automatic rollback, 4) token-level sampling to detect hot sequences and pre-warm cache, 5) better docs for tuning cache and quantization tradeoffs
05:42 Priya: any security risk from enabling token-level sampling? we need sampling to be PII-safe
05:50 Riley: yes, sampling will be PII-safe by default — we hash redacted fields and sample only model input signatures not raw sensitive content. we'll coordinate on retention windows and redaction patterns for your compliance team
06:05 Sonia: timeline — when can we get a canary? we want it before end of month, ideally next week for lower volume test window
06:12 Camila: we can schedule a 48-hour canary starting 2027-09-22; Camila to own scheduling and get you pre-warm config. We'll do a rollback plan and alert thresholds up front
06:30 Jamie: ok, reiterating the short-term fixes we applied: kernel/driver patch rolled to pool, prefix caching enabled, min nodes temporarily increased, triggered automated variant fallback on tail latency; results show 90pct improvement in tail in first 15 minutes after mitigation. we'll send the measured histograms in the packet
06:52 Marcus: great. also, we want a runbook entry for our on-call to know when to ask Redwood for forced fallback vs waiting for autoscaler
07:00 Camila: noted, we'll add a runbook section and an escalation playbook with exact run commands and a contact matrix
07:15 Sonia: pricing impact — increasing min nodes and pre-warm will add cost. can you quantify?
07:23 Riley: yes, we'll run cost delta estimates for the suggested min and pre-warm policy; expect roughly 8-12% uplift for the pre-warm depending on average utilization, we'll include a few scenarios
07:35 Evan: final Q — any dependency on KMS latency that could have affected cache eviction? if KMS calls are slow we might block startup
07:44 Riley: KMS is used for key retrieval on load; we cache keys locally and we saw no KMS latency spikes in the incident timeframe. we'll include the KMS audit in the packet for you to validate
08:00 Jamie: ok, next steps recap: Riley share logs/profiles, Camila schedule canary, Jamie send incident packet + SOC2/KMS docs, Marcus send traffic CSV, and follow-up call next Tuesday same time to review canary results. Anything else?
08:18 Sonia: no that's it, thanks everyone. appreciate the quick turnaround on the patch and the plan
08:25 Jamie: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing within 24 hours

(End)
